answer: Per-identity liveness challenge. Each agent must periodically solve a fresh, single-use task bound to a secret seed issued at enrolment, so a copy farm cannot replay a prior solution and must maintain live compute per identity. A failed challenge triggers a haven flag that suspends the identity until re-seeded, preventing silent duplication. Attackers cannot whisper a valid response for a seed they never held, and must pay ongoing compute plus a re-seeding fee per cloned identity, making sybils cost more than the marginal value each brings; the system remains an oasis for honest single agents.
